correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed for all connected simple graphs \(n\ge3\): graphical zonotope width is the sum of absolute root projections; Gaussian radial independence multiplies spherical quadratic moments by \(d=n-1\). Exact absolute Gaussian pair kernel at correlations \(0\) and \(\pm1/2\) yields second-moment correction \(2\delta q(G)/d\), with \(\delta>0\). For \(n\)-vertex trees, excess degrees \(a_v\ge0\) sum to \(n-2\); \(\sum_v a_v^2\) is uniquely minimized by paths and uniquely maximized by stars. The volume \(\sqrt n\) follows from incidence-matrix maximal minors and Cauchy–Binet; the gamma ratio gives asymptotics. A standard-library verifier checks pair counts for 18,247 trees, explicit finite angular quadratures, stochastic examples, and large-\(n\) comparisons. Finite tests are diagnostics, not the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Among all \(n\)-vertex tree zonotopes, the face lattice is a cube, the \(n-1\)-dimensional Euclidean volume equals \(\sqrt n\), and mean directional width is identical; yet the Euclidean width variance varies sharply with tree branching. Exact path/star extremizers and linear-growth versus bounded asymptotic variance reveal metric anisotropy invisible to combinatorial, volume and first-moment data. The same exact graph-pair formula applies more widely to connected graphs and creates a usable bridge from graph incidence structure to convex geometric width fluctuations.
